title: Glowing Stones of Costa Rica

scenes.query: aerial view of stone spheres field
scenes.text: Hundreds of perfectly round stone spheres line a field

scenes.query: ancient Costa Rican stone spheres closeup
scenes.text: The Diquís Spheres were carved by pre‑Columbian peoples between 700 and 1500 AD.
Many of the spheres are made of granodiorite and glow faintly when wet after rain.
Archaeologists attribute the glow to mineral reactions, but the purpose of the perfectly balanced spheres remains unknown.

scenes.query: mystery symbol call to action graphic

description: Costa Rica’s Diquís Spheres are perfectly round, evenly sized, and sometimes emit a faint glow after rain. Their cultural role is still a mystery. Subscribe for more ancient enigmas.
